# temps_workload_volume (Resource)

A persistent volume of an environment. Attach it to the environment's containers with `temps_workload_volume_attachment`. With `retain_on_delete` the data survives destroying the resource.

Import with `<environment_id>/<id>`.

Required API key permissions: `settings:read`, `settings:write`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "temps_workload_volume" "data" {
  environment_id = temps_environment.production.id
  name           = "data"
  size_mb        = 10240
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `environment_id` (Number) ID of the environment.
- `name` (String) Name of the volume.

### Optional

- `retain_on_delete` (Boolean) Keep the data when the volume is deleted.
- `size_mb` (Number) Size limit in MiB, where the backing supports one.

### Read-Only

- `backing` (String) Where the data lives.
- `id` (String) Import ID, `<environment_id>/<id>`.
- `node_id` (Number) Node the volume is pinned to.
- `volume_id` (Number) Numeric ID of the volume.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <environment_id>/<id>
terraform import temps_workload_volume.data 21/4
```
